name: Kiruna Airport
before:
Sweden's northernmost airport, and the way into the far north of the country. It handled 217,075 passengers in 2023.

Kiruna is a town in the middle of being moved, so the distances are worth getting right: the airport is about 10 km from the old town centre and about 4 km from the new one.

Onward transport runs to the mountains rather than just the town. A transfer bus operated by Falcks Omnibus on behalf of the municipality runs into Kiruna all year for the Stockholm flights. Bus 91 heads once a day to Abisko, Riksgränsen and on to Narvik, roughly February to May and June to September. The Nikkaluoktaexpressen runs once or twice a day on the same seasons to Nikkaluokta.

For the high mountains there are scheduled helicopter flights, including a twice daily summer service from Nikkaluokta to the Kebnekaise mountain lodge, flown by Kallax Flyg.
after:
Sweden's northernmost airport, and the way into the far north of the country. It handled just over 250,000 passengers in 2025.

Kiruna is a town in the middle of being moved, so check which part of town a client is heading for before quoting a transfer.

Onward transport runs to the mountains rather than just the town. An airport coach, run by Kiruna's public transport and operated by Falcks Omnibus, is timed to the flights and runs into central Kiruna. Bus 91 runs between Kiruna and Riksgränsen, and the Nikkaluokta express runs to Nikkaluokta in spring, summer and autumn.

For the high mountains there are scheduled helicopter flights, including Kallax Flyg's route from Nikkaluokta to Kebnekaise.
